nodes.title: ② WHICH one — index from the preview above
reads the clip's real size — wire w/h/length from here
Read me
widgets_values:
REPLACE A SUBJECT — swap in a character.

THREE THINGS TO SET, in order:
  1. TARGET   CLIPTextEncode: what SAM3 should find - 'a man', 'the red car',
              'the woman in the black dress'. Plain words, no syntax.
  2. WHICH    Queue once and look at SAM3_TrackPreview. It numbers every object
              it found. Put the one you want in SAM3_TrackToMask's
              object_indices - '0', or '0,2' for two of them.
  3. RESULT   H3 Scene Prompt: describe who stands there instead. Wire
              H3 Character so it is a specific person, not a generic one.
              Edit the shot line THERE, not on the conditioning node.

SAM3 ONLY - no Florence2, no SAM2
  SAM3 has a text encoder built into the checkpoint
  (detector.backbone.language_backbone.*), so CLIPTextEncode IS the prompt and
  it tracks the subject across frames itself. The older SAM2 route needed
  Florence2 to turn text into boxes first, because SAM2 understands no
  language - two models, an extra failure point, and no tracking.

MODEL FILE
  sam3.1_multiplex_fp16.safetensors, from Comfy-Org/sam3.1, in models/checkpoints.
  sam3.safetensors (SAM 3.0) also loads; ComfyUI detects both. If the dropdown
  does not list it, refresh node definitions (R) - the list is read at startup.

MASK MARGIN
  GrowMaskWithBlur errs generous on purpose. Too tight leaves slivers of the
  original at the edges of fast motion; too loose only costs a little extra
  regeneration.

LENGTH
  Set the conditioning node's length to match your SOURCE clip.

WHY A SPATIAL MASK IS SAFER THAN A TEMPORAL ONE
  Every join cut chased over nine waves sat at a TEMPORAL mask edge and no amount
  of feathering moved it. A spatial edge is a different problem - inpainting
  handles those routinely, because the model sees both sides of the boundary at
  once instead of inventing what comes after a wall in time.

nodes.title: 1. schedule — no source wired, so chunks are just lengths
3b. LATENT PIN — BYPASSED (motion context carries instead)
CHUNKING
widgets_values:
CHUNKED — workflow 14's latent chain

Everything before the chunk layer is a WHOLE-CLIP pass and stays that
way: SAM3, mask stabilise, grow/blur, H3 Match Source and the static
H3 Subject Crop. One crop box for the whole take, or the subject moves
inside the frame at every boundary.

THE CARRY IS THE LATENT CHAIN, the same as the T2V long-form runs:

  H3 Chunk Latent Context sits between H3 Mask Inpaint and the sampler.
  It writes the PREVIOUS chunk's latent tail into this chunk's latent and
  holds it at denoise mask 0, re-applied every step, so those frames come
  out identical. Its `context_length` is the plan's `pin`, which is 0 at
  the first chunk of every shot -- so the chain resets at a cut on its
  own, with no second setting.

  H3 Chunk Close takes the sampler's LATENT as well as the pictures. That
  is what feeds `prev_latent` back to Chunk Open for the next chunk. Without
  that link there is no chain at all.

  No VAE round trip per link, and no pixel-domain context node.

CHUNK OPEN slices four streams on the same boundaries: the cropped video,
its mask, the audio, and the depth on `extra_images`. The depth has to be
sliced too, or every chunk gets the whole clip's depth as its reference
video and the motion guide points at the wrong frames.

chunk_frames 243, context 39 -- the same numbers as the long-form runs.
243 is a legal run and divides by 3, so it lands on both the 24fps video
clock and the 40Hz audio one.

chunk_mode is `scene`: the source is real footage, so let the plan find
its cuts rather than guessing at them.

forget_mask is left wired as you had it. It is inert at forget_strength 0,
which is your setting. If you RAISE that above 0 it will error on a frame
count -- the chunk nodes have one mask slot and cannot slice a second one.

NOT TOUCHED: 20 steps at 0.65, the LoRAs, the mask settings, the crop,
the prompt, the references.
